zh.title: 伊拉克航空重啟出售滯留突尼斯 35 年之兩架波音 747 客機
zh.summary: 伊拉克航空重新出售滯留突尼斯的兩架波音747客機；單架估值提高至90萬美元
body: 伊拉克航空（Iraqi Airways）已重新啟動針對兩架長期停放於突尼斯之波音 747 客機的直接銷售程序。這兩架客機包含一架波音 747-200 與一架罕見的波音 747SP，係於波斯灣戰爭期間飛往突尼斯避難，自此未曾返回伊拉克。歷經約 35 年，兩架飛機至今仍停放於突尼斯西南部的託澤爾-內夫塔國際機場（Tozeur–Nefta International Airport（TOE））。
根據伊拉克航空的最新定價，這兩架大型客機每架估價為 900,000 美元，雙機合計出售總價為 1,800,000 美元。該航空公司曾於 2023 年嘗試出售這兩架客機，當時每架估值為 494,000 美元，但未能售出。時隔三年，伊拉克航空將其估價調高了 82%。

伊拉克航空發布的直接銷售公告顯示，企業與個人買家均可針對單架或兩架客機提出報價。這兩架客機均於 1982 年製造，並列明配備普惠（Pratt & Whitney）JT9D-7F 引擎。意向買家無需支付保證金即可登記意願；獲邀至伊拉克駐突尼斯大使館提交正式報價者，則須提供相當於估值 20% 的保證金（即每架 180,000 美元）。銷售委員會將於 2026 年 12 月 21 日至 2027 年 1 月 5 日期間在該大使館辦理相關手續。
伊拉克航空說明，這兩架客機將按現況出售，不提供任何技術保固。買方須支付成交價 2% 的服務費，並自行負擔所有權轉移、海關清關以及搬遷飛機的費用。在買方完成付款並簽署交接文件後，機場停放費用的支付責任將移轉至買方。
歷史背景方面，伊拉克航空在波斯灣戰爭期間將這兩架波音 747 飛機空渡至託澤爾，以避免受到盟軍空襲破壞。戰後由於國際制裁、長期累積的停放費用以及科威特就佔領期間遭扣押財產進行追討等因素，導致這兩架客機無法返回伊拉克。

en.title: Iraqi Airways Reopens Sale of Two Boeing 747s Stranded in Tunisia for 35 Years
en.summary: Iraqi Airways reopens direct sale of two Boeing 747s stranded in Tunisia, raising valuation to $900,000 each.
body: Iraqi Airways has reopened the direct sale process for two Boeing 747 aircraft that have remained stranded in Tunisia for 35 years. The aircraft, consisting of one Boeing 747-200 and one rare Boeing 747SP, were flown to Tunisia for safekeeping during the Gulf War and never returned to Iraq. Both jumbo jets remain parked at Tozeur–Nefta International Airport (TOE) in southwestern Tunisia.

The Iraqi carrier is offering the aircraft at a valuation of $900,000 per jet, or $1.8 million for the pair. Iraqi Airways previously attempted to sell the two aircraft in 2023 at an estimated value of $494,000 each, but neither aircraft was sold. Three years later, the airline has increased its valuation of the aircraft by 82%.

According to the airline's direct sale notice, both companies and individuals may submit offers for either a single jet or both aircraft. Both aircraft were manufactured in 1982 and are listed as equipped with Pratt & Whitney JT9D-7F engines. Interested buyers may register their interest without putting down a deposit, while those invited to submit a formal offer at the Iraqi Embassy in Tunis must provide a 20% security deposit, amounting to $180,000 per aircraft. The sale committee will be present at the embassy from December 21, 2026, to January 5, 2027.

Iraqi Airways is offering the jets as they stand, without any technical warranty. The successful buyer will be required to pay a 2% service fee on the purchase price and cover all costs for ownership transfer, customs clearance, and moving the aircraft. Responsibility for ongoing parking fees begins after the buyer completes payment and signs the handover documentation.

The two 747s were originally ferried to Tozeur during the Gulf War to keep them out of reach of coalition bombing. Following the war, international sanctions, mounting parking fees, and property recovery claims by Kuwait complicated their return, keeping the long-range jets grounded in Tunisia.
